paragraphs.source_en: But even with the right name, the corporate positioning job isn't done. Your company's name ought to stand for something within your industry. Standing for Something Consider Ford. Everyone knows that Ford is an automobile company. But what kind of car is a Ford? Ford can't build a corporate position on a specific kind of car, because it builds them in all types and all sizes, including trucks. (Whether it should or not is another matter.) Ford had a better idea and switched to its current "Quality is Job 1" campaign. Who owns the "quality" position in automobiles today? Our guess would be MercedesBenz. It never pays to try to take somebody else's position away from them. So the positioning question boils down to some quality to be found across the board in all vehicles. The company has settled on "innovation" as the key attribute in a vehicle from Ford.
